requirement: The compilation_unit production permits the form extern_alias_directive* using_directive* global_attributes? namespace_member_declaration*.
A program may consist of one or more compilation units.

quote_json: "all of the compilation units are processed together"
requirement: Compilation units are processed together so that a unit may depend on declarations in another unit.
Compilation units may depend on one another circularly.
A compilation unit's extern aliases affect its using directives, global attributes, and namespace members.
Extern aliases in one compilation unit do not affect other compilation units.
A compilation unit's using directives affect its global attributes and namespace members.
Using directives in one compilation unit do not affect other compilation units.

quote_json: "attributes for the target assembly and module"
requirement: Compilation-unit global attributes may specify attributes for the target assembly.
notes: See 22.3 for attribute syntax and application rules.

quote_json: "attributes for the target assembly and module"
requirement: Compilation-unit global attributes may specify attributes for the target module.
Assemblies and modules serve as physical containers for declared types.
An assembly may contain multiple physically separate modules.

quote_json: "single declaration space called the global namespace"
requirement: Top-level namespace-member declarations from all compilation units contribute to the same global-namespace declaration space.
The namespace_declaration production permits the form 'namespace' qualified_identifier namespace_body ';'?.
The qualified_identifier production permits the form identifier ('.' identifier)*.
The namespace_body production permits the form '{' extern_alias_directive* using_directive* namespace_member_declaration* '}'.
A namespace may be declared at compilation-unit level and is then a member of the global namespace.
A namespace may be declared within another namespace and is then a member of the enclosing namespace.

quote_json: "name of a namespace shall be unique within the containing namespace"
requirement: A namespace's name must be unique in its containing namespace.
notes: Repeated declarations of the same namespace name denote one namespace under the open-ended rule below; this is uniqueness of the named member, not a ban on reopening it.

requirement: Every namespace is implicitly public.
A namespace declaration cannot contain an access modifier.
Using directives in a namespace body enable direct references to the imported namespace, type, or member names.
notes: See 14.5 for the distinct import kinds and their restrictions.

quote_json: "contribute members to the declaration space of the namespace"
requirement: Namespace-member declarations inside a namespace body add members to that namespace's declaration space.

quote_json: "all using_directives must appear before any member declarations"
requirement: A using directive in a namespace body cannot appear after a member declaration.

quote_json: "define a nested namespace without lexically nesting several namespace declarations"
requirement: A dot-separated namespace declaration name denotes nested namespaces as if the corresponding namespace declarations were lexically nested.
Namespace declarations with the same fully qualified name contribute to one declaration space.
notes: See 7.3; the source points to 7.8.2 for fully qualified names, whose actual definition is in 7.8.3; this allows reopening a namespace.

requirement: An extern alias introduces an identifier for an externally specified namespace.
An extern alias's external namespace specification also covers that namespace's nested namespaces.
The extern_alias_directive production permits the form 'extern' 'alias' identifier ';'.
An extern alias is in scope over using directives, global attributes, and namespace-member declarations of its immediately containing compilation unit or namespace body.
An extern alias identifier may reference its associated namespace within its scope.
An extern alias identifier cannot be global.

quote_json: "only has special meaning when it immediately follows the extern keyword"
requirement: The word alias has contextual-keyword meaning when it immediately follows extern in an extern-alias directive.
notes: See 6.4.4; elsewhere it is an ordinary identifier under the contextual-keyword rules.

requirement: An extern-alias declaration requires a supplied external definition for its alias.
Using directives participate in resolving namespace-or-type names and simple names.
notes: See 7.8 and 12.8.4 for lookup algorithms.

requirement: Using directives do not add members to the enclosing compilation-unit or namespace declaration space.
The using_directive production permits the form using_alias_directive.
The using_directive production permits the form using_namespace_directive.
The using_directive production permits the form using_static_directive.

quote_json: "namespace_member_declarations of its immediately containing compilation unit or namespace body"
requirement: A using directive is in scope over namespace-member declarations in its immediately enclosing compilation unit or namespace body.
notes: Global-attribute scope is stated in 14.2 and 14.5.2.

requirement: A using directive does not affect the resolution of its peer using directives.

quote_json: "order in which they are written is insignificant"
requirement: Reordering peer using directives does not change their meaning.
A using-alias directive may introduce an identifier for a namespace in its immediately enclosing compilation unit or namespace body.
A using-alias directive may introduce an identifier for a type in its immediately enclosing compilation unit or namespace body.
The using_alias_directive production permits the form 'using' identifier '=' namespace_or_type_name ';'.
A using alias may reference its namespace or type from global attributes within the directive's scope.

quote_json: "identifier introduced by the using_alias_directive can be used"
requirement: A using alias may reference its namespace or type from member declarations within the directive's scope.
An extern-alias directive adds no members to the underlying compilation-unit or namespace declaration space.
An extern or using alias is not exported as a member or made available through other bodies reopening the same namespace.
notes: The containing compilation-unit/body scope can naturally include nested declarations.

quote_json: "contributes a name to the alias declaration space"
requirement: Each extern or using alias contributes its name to the immediately enclosing compilation unit's or namespace body's alias declaration space.
notes: See 7.3.

quote_json: "shall be unique within the corresponding alias declaration space"
requirement: Two alias directives in the same alias declaration space cannot introduce the same identifier.

quote_json: "need not be unique within the global declaration space"
requirement: An alias identifier may equal a name in the global or corresponding namespace's member declaration space.
notes: See 14.8.2 for reliable access through '::'.

quote_json: "hidden by similarly named members in nested scopes"
requirement: A member with the same name in a nested scope hides an alias for ordinary name lookup.
notes: Qualified alias lookup is governed by 14.8.1.

requirement: Reordering extern-alias directives in the same compilation unit or namespace body does not change their meaning.

quote_json: "all using_alias_directives must come after all extern_alias_directives"
requirement: A using-alias directive must follow every extern-alias directive in its compilation unit or namespace body.
A using-alias directive's target name is resolved without the alias it is declaring.
A using-alias target name is resolved without other using directives from the immediately containing compilation unit or namespace body.
notes: Using directives in outer containing scopes remain available under ordinary name resolution.

requirement: A using-alias target name is resolved with the extern aliases of its immediately containing compilation unit or namespace body.

quote_json: "including the namespace within which it appears"
requirement: A using alias may name the namespace containing the directive.

quote_json: "any namespace or type nested within that namespace"
requirement: A using alias may name a namespace nested within its containing namespace.

quote_json: "any namespace or type nested within that namespace"
requirement: A using alias may name a type nested within its containing namespace.
Access through an alias resolves to the same namespace or type as access through its declared name.

quote_json: "different extern_alias_directives and using_directives can be present for each part"
requirement: Different parts of a partial type may have different enclosing extern aliases and using directives.
notes: See 15.2.7 for partial types.

requirement: Simple-name resolution in a partial-type part uses only the extern aliases and usings of the namespace bodies and compilation unit enclosing that part.
notes: See 12.8.4; a simple identifier may consequently have different meanings across parts.

requirement: A using alias may name a closed constructed generic type.

quote_json: "cannot name an unbound generic type declaration without supplying type arguments"
requirement: A using alias cannot name an unbound generic type declaration with its type arguments omitted.
A namespace import brings its namespace's direct type members into scope for unqualified type references in the immediately enclosing compilation unit or namespace body.
The using_namespace_directive production permits the form 'using' namespace_name ';'.
A namespace import cannot make its namespace's nested namespaces available as imported unqualified names.
A namespace directive may import a type whose name is already defined in the enclosing compilation unit or namespace body.
A member of the enclosing compilation unit or namespace hides a same-named imported type.
A using alias may select a particular type when namespace imports introduce competing types with that name.

quote_json: "references to that name as a simple_name are considered ambiguous"
requirement: A simple name with competing same-named imported types from peer namespace or static imports is ambiguous.
notes: See 7.8 and 12.8.4 for context, generic arity, hiding, and final lookup; this paragraph states the import conflict.

quote_json: "contain types or members by the same name"
requirement: A simple name with competing same-named imported members or an imported type and member from peer imports is ambiguous.
notes: Open wording question: the referenced 12.8.4 namespace lookup lists namespace-imported types but does not integrate static-imported methods or cross-import method groups; no overload exception is silently added here.

requirement: A namespace-import target is resolved using the same name-resolution environment as a using-alias target.
notes: See 14.5.2: no self or peer using directives, but immediately enclosing extern aliases participate; peer-order independence is also stated in 14.5.1.

quote_json: "nested types and static members contained directly"
requirement: A static import brings the accessible nested types declared directly in its target type into scope for unqualified references in the immediately enclosing unit or namespace body.

quote_json: "identifier of each member and type to be used without qualification"
requirement: A static import brings the accessible non-extension static members declared directly in its target type into scope for unqualified references in the immediately enclosing unit or namespace body.
notes: Accessibility and extension-method restrictions are stated immediately below and in 14.5.4.

requirement: The using_static_directive production permits the form 'using' 'static' type_name ';'.
notes: Open cross-clause question: 7.8.1 and 15.2.2.4.2 omit the using-static target from their permitted static-class name contexts, despite the import permission here; retain this production without inventing an exception in another clause.

quote_json: "does not import extension methods directly as static methods"
requirement: An extension method cannot be referenced as an unqualified static method solely through a static import of its declaring type.
A static import makes its target type's extension methods available for extension-method invocation.
notes: See 12.8.9.3 for extension-method lookup and invocation rules.

quote_json: "not members and types declared in base classes"
requirement: A static import cannot supply an unqualified member reference to a static member declared only in a base class.

quote_json: "only imports members and types declared directly"
requirement: A static import cannot supply an unqualified type reference to a nested type declared only in a base class.
The namespace_member_declaration production permits the form namespace_declaration.
The namespace_member_declaration production permits the form type_declaration.

quote_json: "A compilation unit or a namespace body can contain"
requirement: Namespace-member declarations in a compilation unit contribute members to the global declaration space.

quote_json: "contribute new members to the underlying declaration space"
requirement: Namespace-member declarations in a namespace body contribute members to that namespace's declaration space.
The type_declaration production permits the form class_declaration.
notes: See 15.2, 16.2, 18.2, 19.2, and 20.2 for syntax and constraints on each type-declaration form.

requirement: The type_declaration production permits the form struct_declaration.
notes: See 15.2, 16.2, 18.2, 19.2, and 20.2 for syntax and constraints on each type-declaration form.

requirement: The type_declaration production permits the form interface_declaration.
notes: See 15.2, 16.2, 18.2, 19.2, and 20.2 for syntax and constraints on each type-declaration form.

requirement: The type_declaration production permits the form enum_declaration.
notes: See 15.2, 16.2, 18.2, 19.2, and 20.2 for syntax and constraints on each type-declaration form.

requirement: The type_declaration production permits the form delegate_declaration.
notes: See 15.2, 16.2, 18.2, 19.2, and 20.2 for syntax and constraints on each type-declaration form.

requirement: A type declaration may occur at compilation-unit level.
A type declaration may occur as a namespace member.
A type declaration may occur as a class member.
A type declaration may occur as a struct member.
A compilation-unit-level type declaration's fully qualified name equals its unqualified name.
notes: The source points to 7.8.2 for both names, but 7.8.2 defines unqualified names and 7.8.3 defines fully qualified names; the stated equality remains clear.

requirement: A type declaration within a namespace, class, or struct has fully qualified name S.N, with S the container's fully qualified name and N the type's unqualified name.
notes: The quote preserves the PDF's missing space; the printed paragraph points to 7.8.3 for the fully qualified name and 7.8.2 for the unqualified name.

requirement: A type declared within a class or struct is a nested type.
A type declared in compilation units or namespaces may have public access.
notes: See 7.5.2 for accessibility definitions.

requirement: A type declared in compilation units or namespaces may have internal access.
notes: See 7.5.2 for accessibility definitions.

requirement: A type declared in compilation units or namespaces without an access modifier has internal access.

quote_json: "Types declared in compilation units or namespaces"
requirement: A type declared in compilation units or namespaces cannot use an access level outside the listed set: public, internal.
notes: The preceding sentence introduces these as the permitted access modifiers.

requirement: A type declared in classes may have public access.
notes: See 7.5.2 for accessibility definitions.

requirement: A type declared in classes may have protected internal access.
notes: See 7.5.2 for accessibility definitions.

requirement: A type declared in classes may have protected access.
notes: See 7.5.2 for accessibility definitions.

requirement: A type declared in classes may have private protected access.
notes: See 7.5.2 for accessibility definitions.

requirement: A type declared in classes may have internal access.
notes: See 7.5.2 for accessibility definitions.

requirement: A type declared in classes may have private access.
notes: See 7.5.2 for accessibility definitions.

requirement: A type declared in classes without an access modifier has private access.
A type declared in classes cannot use an access level outside the listed set: public, protected internal, protected, private protected, internal, private.
notes: The preceding sentence introduces these as the permitted access modifiers.

requirement: A type declared in structs may have public access.
notes: See 7.5.2 for accessibility definitions.

requirement: A type declared in structs may have internal access.
notes: See 7.5.2 for accessibility definitions.

requirement: A type declared in structs may have private access.
notes: See 7.5.2 for accessibility definitions.

requirement: A type declared in structs without an access modifier has private access.
A type declared in structs cannot use an access level outside the listed set: public, internal, private.
notes: The preceding sentence introduces these as the permitted access modifiers.

quote_json: "looked up only as an extern or using alias"
requirement: A non-global identifier to the left of '::' is looked up only as an extern or using alias, unaffected by ordinary type or member names.
notes: The special global identifier is specified below.

requirement: A qualified alias member can access a namespace alias even when ordinary lookup would hide it behind another entity.
A qualified alias member can explicitly access the global namespace.
The qualified_alias_member production permits the form identifier '::' identifier type_argument_list?.
A qualified alias member may be used as a namespace-or-type name.
notes: See 7.8.

requirement: A qualified alias member may be the left operand of a member access.

quote_json: "global namespace is searched for the right-hand identifier"
requirement: When the left identifier of '::' is global, lookup of the right identifier starts in the global namespace.

quote_json: "that namespace is searched for the right-hand identifier"
requirement: When the first alias found for a non-global left identifier of '::' denotes a namespace, lookup of the right identifier searches only that namespace.
notes: The ordered search in the following decision list stops at that alias, including when its right member is missing.

requirement: A non-global qualified alias member requires a matching extern or using alias for its left identifier.
A non-global qualified alias member is a compile-time error when the first alias found for its left identifier in the prescribed scope search denotes a type.
notes: The first alias stops lookup; a namespace alias in an outer scope is not tried, as the following decision list states.

requirement: A qualified alias member with type arguments has the form N::I<A1, ..., Ae> with at least one type argument.
notes: N and I are identifiers; e denotes supplied generic arity in the lookup rules below.

requirement: A qualified alias member without type arguments has the form N::I and uses arity zero in lookup.

quote_json: "namespace named I and e is zero"
requirement: Global-qualified lookup resolves to a global namespace member named I when the supplied arity is zero and that member exists.

quote_json: "non-generic type named I and e is zero"
requirement: If the namespace branch does not apply, global-qualified lookup resolves to a global non-generic type named I when the supplied arity is zero.
If the preceding global branches do not apply, global-qualified lookup resolves to the type named I with the supplied arity, constructed with the given type arguments.
notes: Generic type-argument validity is governed by the referenced type rules, not restated here.

requirement: Global-qualified lookup is a compile-time error if none of its namespace, non-generic-type, or matching-arity type branches applies.
Non-global qualified-alias lookup searches the immediately containing namespace, each enclosing namespace from inner to outer, and finally the containing compilation unit until an alias is located.
notes: The PDF's indentation distinguishes this loop from the final failure branch.

quote_json: "namespace named I and e is zero"
requirement: Namespace-alias-qualified lookup resolves to a nested namespace named I when the supplied arity is zero and that namespace exists.

quote_json: "non-generic type named I and e is zero"
requirement: If its namespace branch does not apply, namespace-alias-qualified lookup resolves to a non-generic type named I in the aliased namespace when the supplied arity is zero.

quote_json: "type named I that has e type parameters"
requirement: If its preceding branches do not apply, namespace-alias-qualified lookup resolves to the type named I in the aliased namespace with matching arity, constructed with the given type arguments.
Once a namespace alias is found, qualified lookup is a compile-time error if its namespace has no applicable namespace, non-generic-type, or matching-arity type member.
notes: An outer alias is not tried after this failure.

quote_json: "as long as it is used only with the :: qualifier"
requirement: An alias sharing a type or namespace name cannot be used as that alias without the '::' qualifier.
notes: Separate alias declaration space and uniqueness repeat 14.5.2; a type alias cannot itself be used to the left of '::' under 14.8.1.

quote_json: "The identifier of a using-alias-directive must be unique within the declaration space"
requirement: An alias identifier must differ from a member name in the immediately containing compilation-unit or namespace declaration space, even if the alias is unused.
notes: Per-test observations of the disagreement are recorded in departures.tsv. Positive witnesses demonstrate the construct's prerequisites; failing originals do not prove mutation sensitivity.

requirement: Top-level statements must precede namespace member declarations in their compilation unit.
notes: Committee prose read at both registered pins before proposal; registered csc is the authority.

requirement: Types following a file-scoped namespace belong to the named namespace, with ordinary namespace-relative name lookup.
notes: Committee prose read at both registered pins before proposal; registered csc is the authority.

requirement: A using alias following a file-scoped namespace has namespace-body scope, taking precedence over an outer alias with the same name.
notes: Committee prose read at both registered pins before proposal; registered csc is the authority.

requirement: A source file cannot declare more than one file-scoped namespace.
notes: Committee prose read at both registered pins before proposal; registered csc is the authority.

requirement: A source file cannot combine a file-scoped namespace with a block namespace.
notes: Committee prose read at both registered pins before proposal; registered csc is the authority.

requirement: A type declaration cannot precede a file-scoped namespace declaration.
notes: Committee prose read at both registered pins before proposal; registered csc is the authority.

requirement: A compilation unit cannot combine a file-scoped namespace with top-level statements.
notes: Committee prose read at both registered pins before proposal; registered csc is the authority.

quote_json: "Namespaces whose names begin with System. are reserved for use by the Standard Library"
requirement: Namespaces whose names begin with System. are reserved for the Standard Library.
notes: The reservation concerns namespace provenance; it is not a blanket prohibition on the name System itself.
